title: ÆTHER: Kolusu v2 (anklet bells, wind, water, deep-sea call)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: Terrifying South Indian horror film background score, instrumental, 75 seconds: a vengeful ghost in an old village house by a deep well at midnight. Written the way Tamil and Telugu horror film composers write it, not a Western horror cue. Second zero, totally alone and loud, right next to the ear: heavy silver anklet bells (kolusu, many tiny jingling bells on an ankle) shaking with slow walking footsteps, jingle, jingle, stop. Then a cold howling wind through a broken window, rising and moaning. At 4 seconds a deep, slow, haunting whale-like moaning call, pitched very low like a giant creature from the deep ocean, long and sliding, the ghost's voice. A lone close female voice hums a slow eerie lullaby, wordless, in a dark raga (minor second, raised fourth, minor sixth, raised seventh) with long sliding bends; it starts with a rising three-note call (root, minor third, fifth, last note bent up). The anklet bells keep jingling all through the whole track as the rhythm, like the hi-hat of the groove, always clearly heard. From about 8 seconds one layer at a time: dripping water echoing in a stone well, an out-of-tune veena plucked and stuttering, a low mridangam thump like something heavy behind a door, bowed metal and scraping cello clusters, a slow ritual hourglass drum. At 18 seconds the wind stops dead, one second of total silence, then a huge sudden water SPLASH as something falls into the well, together with a massive jump-scare stinger: screaming high strings and a huge low hit. Then the possession ritual: fast frantic triplet drum gallop with thavil and ritual drum, the anklet bells shaking wildly in rhythm, tight full-band unison stabs with deep brass and distorted strings, a wordless male chant growling, the deep whale-like moan returning under the lullaby melody played huge on low brass, the wind howling louder, a new terrifying idea every 8 to 10 seconds. At about 45 seconds everything drops to the anklet bells walking slowly closer, the wind and the humming a whole step higher, the deep whale call groaning, water dripping, for six seconds, never silent. One beat of total silence. Then the biggest jump scare: a giant slam with every instrument, another huge water splash, a shrieking choir cluster and pounding triplet drums, a rhythmic phrase played three times landing hard. Ending: the anklet bells jingle twice right at the ear, the wind dies, the three-note lullaby call hummed once, then a sudden cut. Real acoustic instruments and real sounds (anklet bells, wind, water) carry half the sound, dark processed electronics the other half. No silence longer than one second. Huge dynamic range, deep sub bass, wide cinematic mix. No lyrics, no spoken words, no EDM, no generic Hollywood trailer braams, no white-noise risers.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct: 'i need a horror track, it should kill the person and burn the ass', i.e. the scariest possible horror BGM. Horror the South Indian film way (style, rule 15): a ghost's lullaby melody in a dark raga (Subhapantuvarali-like: minor second, raised fourth, minor sixth, raised seventh) hummed by one female voice with slow gamakam bends; anklet bells (kolusu) as the ghost's footsteps = our own sound palette (rule 9); the udukkai hourglass drum of village possession rituals; the possession frenzy switching into a tisram triplet gallop with tight full-band unison stabs; stop-and-slam jump scares; a korvai ending played three times. Broken Heritage: reversed veena = the creeping riser (once), pitched-down mridangam = the sub thumps, glitch-chopped veena stutters like a flickering lamp. Motif: the lullaby begins with the rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, bent up) and the track ends on it. Rules 9.11-9.13: one-two sounds open with an instant attention grab, layer by layer, a new event every 8-12 s, two composed jump scares (full silence then a slam) plus a key lift. Horror needs real dynamic range, so mastering keeps the silences (no heavy squash). v2 (Jithesh 29 Oct 17:27 on take 1): 'the sounds of kolusu are not there'; add a scary wind, a splash of water, and a mystery sound like a deep ocean whale. So: the anklet bells are now the FIRST sound alone and become the hi-hat of the whole groove (heard all through, not a passing colour); a howling wind through a broken window is the bed and the riser; a sudden water splash (something dropped into a well) is the first jump scare; a deep, slow, whale-like moaning call pitched far down is the ghost's voice and the mystery hook. Take 1 had ~10 s of near silence before the last slam, so the silences are capped at 1 s.

story: Midnight in an old ancestral house in a village. A swing creaks on its own, anklet bells walk across the empty hall, a woman hums a lullaby nobody should know. The lamp goes out. She is right behind you.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
